claims.title: Snippet ancestor check searches the whole document, so snippets are never extracted
claims.text:
🟡 **P2**

**Snippet ancestor check searches the whole document, so snippets are never extracted**

`RESULT_ANCHOR` starts with `//`. In lxml, `element.xpath("//a...")` is evaluated from the document root, not from `parent`. `parent.xpath(RESULT_ANCHOR)` therefore returns every result anchor on the page (8 in the fixture), `len(...) != 1` is always true, and the loop breaks on the first iteration. `node` stays the `<a>` itself. `content` is then just the anchor's text (the site name and breadcrumb) minus the title and `<cite>` text, for example "Python documentation", rather than the result description.

Use a relative expression for this check (`"." + RESULT_ANCHOR`, i.e. `.//a[...]`). Separately, in the fixture layout the snippet sits in a sibling `div.kb0PBd` under `div.N54PNb`. That is 5 levels above the anchor, and `MAX_SNIPPET_ANCESTORS` is 4, so the depth limit also needs checking against the real DOM.

No test asserts on `content`, so the 9 passing tests do not catch this.

<!-- ai-review:fp=bug|integrations/searxng/stealth_google.py|68674a6e49c59e95.0 -->

claims.title: Zero results without the interstitial is returned silently
claims.text:
🟡 **P2**

**Zero results without the interstitial is returned silently**

When the page has no `/goto` result anchors and no interstitial text, `response()` returns an empty `EngineResults` with nothing logged. A Google block or "unusual traffic" page, a CAPTCHA the gateway failed to solve, or a layout change that breaks `RESULT_ANCHOR` all look like a search with no hits. The only distinguishable failure today is the interstitial. The README and spec list an unresolved "unexpected crash" and a 423 `blocked` case, and this path would hide a recurrence. Log a warning here (or raise `SearxEngineAPIException`) with context such as the page title and body length, so a parser or layout break can be told apart from a real empty result.

<!-- ai-review:fp=bug|integrations/searxng/stealth_google.py|ecb5588c53f6631b.0 -->

claims.title: Missing env vars surface as a bare KeyError
claims.text:
🟡 **P2**

**Missing env vars surface as a bare KeyError**

If `STEALTH_BROWSER_URL` or `STEALTH_BROWSER_TOKEN` is unset, which is the exact failure mode of the wiring the docs say was lost on the cluster, `request()` raises `KeyError: 'STEALTH_BROWSER_URL'`. SearXNG reports this as an unexpected engine crash, which does not say what to fix. Raise `SearxEngineAPIException` or `RuntimeError` with a message naming the variable and the engine, e.g. 'stealth google engine requires STEALTH_BROWSER_URL'.

<!-- ai-review:fp=bug|integrations/searxng/stealth_google.py|f0ef6eac8c86c3b9.0 -->

claims.title: Empty or non-HTML gateway body crashes with an opaque lxml error
claims.text:
🟢 **P3**

**Empty or non-HTML gateway body crashes with an opaque lxml error**

`html.fromstring` raises `lxml.etree.ParserError` ('Document is empty') on an empty body, and can also fail on a non-HTML payload such as a JSON error from the gateway. Neither is handled, so the failure surfaces as a generic engine crash with no mention of the gateway. Guard with a check on `resp.text`, or catch the lxml error and re-raise `SearxEngineAPIException('gateway returned an unparseable body')`.

<!-- ai-review:fp=bug|integrations/searxng/stealth_google.py|d1e1edbd5d58140c.0 -->

claims.title: README records a transient deployment state that will rot
claims.text:
🟢 **P3**

**README records a transient deployment state that will rot**

Known issue 2 describes the state of one session's cluster on 2026-11-03: an overwritten deploy and lost env vars, mount and settings entry. It also says this has not been rechecked. A README in the gateway repo should not carry a claim like this. It becomes false once openclaw-setup is redeployed, and nobody will know to remove it. The same applies to "Last run: 9 passed" at line 42, which goes stale as soon as a test is added or removed. Move the deployment status to an issue or the PR description and drop the test count. The README can point to the test command alone.

<!-- ai-review:fp=nitpick|integrations/searxng/README.md|7c0081bdf572fe00.0 -->

claims.title: Spec open items cite a transcript and plan that are not in the repo
claims.text:
🟢 **P3**

**Spec open items cite a transcript and plan that are not in the repo**

Two open items justify themselves by what "the transcript" does or does not show. They also lean on "the plan", which is not part of this PR. A later maintainer has no way to check either source. Each item should state the action as a self-contained check, for example "confirm the engine path with `kubectl exec ... ls /usr/local/searxng/searx/engines`" and "run python-reviewer on the engine". The references to unavailable artifacts can then be dropped.

<!-- ai-review:fp=nitpick|docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-03-searxng-google-engine-design.md|c5e22c8c74999765.0 -->

claims.title: Empty noise fragment garbles the snippet text
claims.text:
🟡 **P2**

**Empty noise fragment garbles the snippet text**

`str.replace("", " ")` inserts a space between every character. If a result has an empty `<h3>` or an empty `<cite>`, `_text()` returns `""` and `noise` contains an empty string. The whole snippet then comes out spaced between each character. Skip empty fragments before replacing.

*Suggested fix:*

```suggestion
    for fragment in filter(None, noise):
```

claims.title: Deployment note is attached to known issue 1
claims.text:
🟢 **P3**

**Deployment note is attached to known issue 1**

The new line follows item 1 with no blank line and no list marker. Markdown treats it as a lazy continuation of item 1, so it reads as part of the interstitial issue. It is not a known issue itself. Put it in its own paragraph after a blank line, or move it out of the Known issues list.

*Suggested fix:*

```suggestion

Deployment status lives with the `openclaw-setup` wiring, not in this repo.
```
